turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Margaret Byrne, come on through. I'll get your blood pressure before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. Sean, you come in with me. We circled that car park twice, it's a pure disgrace.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We did, yeah. I'll sit over by the wall and stay quiet.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Sleeve up, please, and keep the arm still.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): This cardigan is a nuisance, hang on. Did ye see the match? The referee was desperate.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 148 over 86, and the pulse is 74. I'll leave it on the screen.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Morning Margaret. Routine review of the blood pressure and the cholesterol. Any chest pain?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The roses are black after the rain, I've done nothing in the garden. No, no chest pain.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any breathlessness? Any dizziness?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm well able for the hill up to the church.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): You're on atorvastatin for the cholesterol and ramipril for the blood pressure, yes?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I stopped the atorvastatin, the 20 milligram cholesterol tablet. I read a thing online, your man said they destroy the muscles, so I left it off.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did you stop it?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Sean has the diabetes, and he's on the metformin, two tablets with his dinner. I hide the biscuits up high.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's Sean's tablet, not yours. When did you yourself stop the atorvastatin?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, sorry. A month ago... no, more like five or six weeks ago. After that article.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She put the box up in the press and that was the end of it. She was worried, right enough.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the ramipril, are you taking that every day?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the ten milligram... no, wait, the box says five milligrams. I take it every other day. I feel grand, so every day seems a bit much.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): It was prescribed once a day. Are you steady at every other day, or is it hit and miss?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Every other day, I suppose. Sometimes I forget which day I'm on.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She has the alarm and she switches it off. I wouldn't swear it's every second day.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any muscle pains while you were on the statin?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. The knee is at me if I kneel weeding, but that's the old arthritis, nothing new.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any swelling of the ankles?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not a bit.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bowels or waterworks giving you any trouble?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No, all grand on that front. We had a lovely bit of fish on Friday, if that's not too much information.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I never smoked in my life. Sean gave them up, which is more than I can say for the biscuit tin.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Leave the biscuits. My metformin is a thousand milligrams, one at breakfast and one with the tea, not two at dinner. She always mixes that up.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's your medicine, Sean, we'll leave it. Margaret, the pressure today is up a shade, which fits with skipping the ramipril.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't want to be swallowing tablets for the sake of it. That website had me pure worried, people who could barely walk.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to lecture you. We'll repeat the bloods, a fasting cholesterol and a kidney test, and we'll look at the statin again in a month.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to starve? Last time I was raging, no breakfast and the queue out the door.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, fasting from the night before for the cholesterol. The kidney bloods are the same morning. Don't restart the atorvastatin until we've seen them.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get her there. She cancelled the last appointment for bloods and said nothing to me.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take the five milligram ramipril every morning, not every other day.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Every morning. Even Sundays?
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Every day, Sundays included. If you feel light-headed, sit down and ring the surgery, but don't just drop doses.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister says cinnamon drops the cholesterol. Will I pick some up in the chemist?
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): No, leave the cinnamon. It won't do the job of a statin if the numbers are up.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Fair enough. The paracetamol I take now and again for the knee, that's alright to continue?
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, paracetamol when you need it is fine. No more than eight tablets in a day.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I can book those bloods for Thursday morning at the desk, fasting from Wednesday night.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday is bingo, but I'll go early. Sean will drop me down.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. I'll see you back in a month with the results and we'll decide then about the cholesterol tablet.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand, we'll be there. Thanks, doctor. Mind yourself.

omissions.text: Ramipril dosing was recorded incompletely/wrongly: the patient initially thought it was 10 mg but then confirmed the box says 5 mg, and the doctor specifically instructed her to take ramipril 5 mg every morning once daily.
Patient denied muscle pains attributable to atorvastatin; she said no real muscle pains, only longstanding knee pain from old arthritis and nothing new while on the statin.

The patient reported reduced medication adherence beyond simple alternate-day use: she said she sometimes forgets which day she is on, and her family member said he would not swear she even takes ramipril every second day.
The patient had cancelled the last blood test appointment, per family member.
Doctor advised reviewing/deciding about restarting the cholesterol tablet after blood results at the 1-month follow-up, not to restart before then.
